hidden_run_story_state.taboo: do not name the dead after dusk
hidden_run_story_state.hope: eastward ascent to the lit terraces

recurring_motifs: blue cord knots marking safe household routes
seven-bowl sharing sets for households larger than their utensils
eastward arrows scratched beside sheltered niches
covered names with age marks left visible
water-measure lines repurposed as ration and child-growth marks

nook_packets.survival_use: family sleeping shelf hidden behind a broken water screen
nook_packets.material_context: wet stone, patched reed mats, bowl stack, wind cloth tied to cracked bronze rings
nook_packets.survival_pressure: crowding and the need to hide dependents near water access
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: children sleep furthest from the outer edge and no voice rises above a whisper after the second lantern
evidence_objects: three layered bedroll nests
seven chipped bowls for one household
waterline marks reused as child-height marks
blue cord tied around the safest sleeping corner
text_fragments: Third ledge holds two. Do not take the mat if you are leaving before dawn.
Blue cord on the left post means the water below is still drawn.
Mark your count on the stone. Caretaker checks at first bell.
symbol_fragments: three short chalk lines repeated beside the smallest bedroll
bowl arrangement from smallest to largest sleeper
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: one bedroll niche is warm-shaped but empty, with its bowl turned upside down.
nook_packets.location_hint: under the first terrace stair where runoff still reaches the stone lip
nook_packets.voice_note: Caretaker voice: the ledge is managed infrastructure, not refuge, and the phrasing enforces that distinction under scarcity.

nook_packets.survival_use: household votive shelf for asking silence and concealment
nook_packets.material_context: soot-black alcove, wax drips, broken lamp cups reused as offering bowls
nook_packets.survival_pressure: fear that speaking too freely brings tribunal attention and invites loss
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: a vow is knotted, not spoken, if the bridge below still carries listeners
evidence_objects: wax pooled in old lamp cups
rope-knotted petitions instead of written names
erased saint face with only the hands left visible
text_fragments: One wick per household. Do not light for the unnamed.
Age only. No name after dusk. This was agreed.
Seven bowls. Three remain. Do not move the arrangement.
symbol_fragments: three blue knots tied around a lamp hook
soot cross-lines covering an older blessing
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: the central name plaque has been scraped smooth, but finger-polish remains where people still touch it.
nook_packets.location_hint: halfway up the intake wall between two collapsed lantern brackets
nook_packets.voice_note: Mourner voice enforcing the taboo against naming the dead after dusk, with the bowl-count as a grief tally that doubles as inventory.

nook_packets.survival_use: quiet maintenance corner for bridge-line repairs and covert route marking
nook_packets.material_context: scarred plank, bronze hook fragments, chalk measures on stone, snapped pulley tooth
nook_packets.survival_pressure: bridge travel must continue without attracting customs scrutiny or total structural failure
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: never replace two public lines in the same watch
evidence_objects: chalk splice lengths
bundle of mismatched cord
hook sorted by load size
half-finished replacement pin
text_fragments: Blue cord spliced here must hold forty spans before the next anchor.
Novice: do not cut short to save time. The captain will know.
Eastward lines are priority. Mark them twice.
symbol_fragments: load arrows with one safe path bent eastward
crossed-out measure where original cord thickness is impossible
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: the strongest replacement rope is gone, but the weak public-looking rope remains in place.
nook_packets.location_hint: beside the old scaffold market drop where carriers once rebalanced loads
nook_packets.voice_note: Work captain instruction left for a novice, practical and slightly threatening, tied to the eastward-ascent route motif.

nook_packets.survival_use: hidden issue point for household shares and emergency reductions
nook_packets.material_context: sealed jars, weight stones, scraped tally wall, cloth plugs against damp
nook_packets.survival_pressure: food is low and official measures no longer match real mouths
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: the old toll weights may be read but never trusted
evidence_objects: three jar sizes color-marked by chalk
stones grouped by child, elder, worker
tally wall where public and private counts diverge
text_fragments: Twelve measures in. Seven spoken for. Do not touch the bottom row.
Water-line at the third mark is the household share. Not the carrier share.
If the seal is broken and you did not break it, go east. Now.
symbol_fragments: double tally system, one bold and one hidden under soot
jar caps turned east for reserve stock
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: the official ledger shelf is empty, but the chalk beneath it records more people than the tax niche was built to feed.
nook_packets.linked_motif: water measure reused as ration law
nook_packets.location_hint: inside a cracked retaining wall near the intake arch
nook_packets.voice_note: Quartermaster voice: the recess is a rationed store, and the final line encodes the survival doctrine of concealment as an emergency instruction.

nook_packets.survival_use: covered memorial for those who died during the first poison nights
nook_packets.material_context: ash jars, wrapped bundles, linen strips over names, apology offerings of dried herbs
nook_packets.survival_pressure: grief must be preserved without breaking the dusk naming taboo
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: after dusk, ages may be counted but names must be veiled
evidence_objects: three ash jars with cloth veils
age marks carved beside hidden names
one child-height token tied to an adult jar
text_fragments: Veil stays until the seventh morning. Do not lift it to check.
Age: 44. Age: 9. Age: 9.
We do not say them here. We said them at the east terrace.
symbol_fragments: smallest age marks clustered nearest the wall
veils tied with the same blue cord seen on safe routes
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: one jar space is empty and still ringed by fresh ash, as if the body never stayed long enough to cool.
nook_packets.location_hint: behind the intake customs altar where old service vessels were once stored
nook_packets.voice_note: Mourner voice: the ages without names honor the taboo while the repeated child-age makes the loss legible without exposition.

nook_packets.survival_use: daytime schooling and sewing corner for the smallest children
nook_packets.material_context: shallow step basin, thread scraps, chalk copy lines, folded cloth dolls without faces
nook_packets.survival_pressure: children must remain quiet, occupied, and ready to move fast
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: copy the rule until your hand knows it better than your mouth
evidence_objects: chalk copy lines at knee height
tiny folded cloth dolls missing mouths
needle wrap hidden under a basin lip
text_fragments: Water here is not for drinking. Do not let the children forget.
Ration line is the third scratch from the drain. Below that, report to the caretaker.
Soap left means someone is coming back. Do not use it.
symbol_fragments: child-sized arrows all pointing to the same hidden stair
practice tally marks that stop midway across the stone
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: one copy line breaks off after the word 'mother' and is smeared by a wet hand.
nook_packets.location_hint: on the dry bath step above the cracked basin drain
nook_packets.voice_note: Caretaker voice with a refugee clerk's precision: the soap line encodes hope and absence simultaneously without naming either.

nook_packets.former_use: toll icon and customs seal shelf
nook_packets.survival_use: contested devotional and legal nook where rule and mercy are argued in marks
nook_packets.material_context: stamp trays, seal wax, scratched exemptions, candle stubs set in tax weights
nook_packets.survival_pressure: old gate law still controls movement, but household survival requires exemptions no authority can cleanly grant
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: do not stamp a child as cargo, even if the bridge demands a count
evidence_objects: old customs stamp beside melted votive wax
small ledger shards with rewritten entries
weights used as candle holders
text_fragments: Toll ledger closed at the poisoning. These marks are ours now.
Blue cord tied to the left bracket: safe passage confirmed this morning.
Do not move the icon. The guard uses it to count who has passed.
symbol_fragments: official seal crossed by a hand-drawn lantern
same line entered twice, once in rule-script and once in hurried household shorthand
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: the heaviest stamp is gone, but its clean square remains in the dust.
nook_packets.location_hint: inside the customs alcove overlooking the first bridge gate
nook_packets.voice_note: Guard voice repurposing official toll infrastructure for concealed household route-signaling, showing the rupture event's administrative aftermath.

nook_packets.survival_use: reserve cache for households planning an eastward break
nook_packets.material_context: low stone tunnel, sealed jars, wrapped dried roots, blue knot markers on the third brick seam
nook_packets.survival_pressure: public stores are watched; any real escape needs hidden food and dry cloth
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: never empty the reserve in one crossing
evidence_objects: three reserve jars behind removable stone
bundle of dry wraps
chalk count on tunnel ceiling visible only when lying down
text_fragments: Three jars. The cracked one is not food. Do not open it in here.
If you are reading this and you are not from the terrace households, leave one jar and go.
Mark on the lid means it was tested. No mark means wait for the caretaker.
symbol_fragments: third-brick blue knot code
ceiling marks for number of crossings supplied
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: one jar ring is empty and recently swept clean, but no new count replaces it.
nook_packets.location_hint: under the drain lip beneath the second terrace bridge
nook_packets.voice_note: Scavenger voice with a refugee clerk's caution: the cracked jar implies the poisoning without naming it, and the conditional address enforces concealment doctrine.

nook_packets.survival_use: memorial stop for those taken when the warning bells failed
nook_packets.material_context: frayed bell rope, charcoal wall marks, stacked token stones, one snapped clapper shard
nook_packets.survival_pressure: many deaths came from route failure and delayed warning rather than open battle
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: the blind bell is touched once for each household lost, never rung
evidence_objects: token stone stacks by household
rope polished by silent touch
charcoal marks for each failed watch
text_fragments: Bell is not rung after dusk. This was decided.
Scratch a line for each household that passed through. Forty-one lines.
Do not ask who stopped counting.
symbol_fragments: watch marks split into before-poison and after-poison counts
one child's token nested inside a larger stack
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: the clapper is gone, but the rope is more worn than any active bell line nearby.
nook_packets.location_hint: at the blind side of the collapsed bell station above the intake run
nook_packets.voice_note: Mourner voice compressed to near-silence: the tally and the unanswered question carry the grief without any ornament.

nook_packets.survival_use: mixed-use bench where plant care techniques were repurposed into splinting and rope patching
nook_packets.material_context: pruning grooves, twine, reed splints, bronze knife with root sap and lamp soot on the same edge
nook_packets.survival_pressure: old garden craft survives only by being turned toward bodies, ropes, and concealment
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: good binding is used first for the living, then for the wall
evidence_objects: grafting knife reused for cord trimming
reed splints cut to forearm length
old plant labels turned into measure tabs
text_fragments: Eastward rootstock only. The western beds are not worth the water.
Child's copy: graft at the third node, bind with the thin cord, do not touch for nine days.
If it takes, mark the pot with a line. If it does not, say nothing.
symbol_fragments: former plant rows crossed into limb-length marks
sap stains overlapping repair chalk
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: the table still has labeled garden pegs, but no living grafts remain nearby.
nook_packets.linked_motif: former use survives through body care
nook_packets.location_hint: on a terrace spur where the old hanging beds once caught runoff
nook_packets.voice_note: Work captain instruction transcribed by a child into a copy exercise, with the eastward-ascent hope embedded in the agricultural priority.

nook_packets.survival_use: teaching nook where children learn route law and silence practice before crossings
nook_packets.material_context: curtain veil, chalk panel, low stool, hidden bundle of spare wraps
nook_packets.survival_pressure: every child must know the route rules before their first concealed crossing
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: you may point east before you may say east
evidence_objects: chalk panel with erased route lesson
low stool worn into one corner
spare wraps measured to child height
text_fragments: Copy until the line is straight. Caretaker will check the angle.
Do not write names. Write ages. Write directions. Write counts.
Eastward arrow: draw it the same way every time. This matters.
symbol_fragments: rows of hand-drawn arrows with only one left un-crossed
small handprints stopping at the safe edge line
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: the final lesson panel is washed clean except for one eastward arrow at the bottom.
nook_packets.location_hint: behind the veil on the stair just before the customs overlook
nook_packets.voice_note: Novice and child voice in a constrained lesson environment where the curriculum is survival literacy, not letters.

nook_packets.survival_use: rapid-wrap station for bodies that could not be kept in open household space
nook_packets.material_context: tool hooks, ash cloth, lime bowl, hurried knot wraps, one official hook still labeled for bridge irons
nook_packets.survival_pressure: poison deaths came too quickly for full rites and too openly for public mourning
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: if the body crosses before dusk, the name waits until morning
evidence_objects: stacked ash cloth wraps
lime bowl beside old iron hook labels
bundle tags marked by age and household count instead of name
text_fragments: Ash wrap means the household is finished. Do not disturb the bundle.
Penitent: if you wrapped it, you owe three days of water-carrying. No exceptions.
Age marked on the outside. Name is inside. It stays inside.
symbol_fragments: bundle tags grouped by family knot pattern
hook labels overwritten with ash counts
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: one wrap is tied but empty, as if a body was taken back by its household after the count was made.
nook_packets.location_hint: in the tool bay beneath the main customs bridge
nook_packets.voice_note: Penitent and mourner voice: the ash wrap is a burial practice shaped entirely by the taboo, with the name's concealment made physically literal.
